alignments.note: Construct noun with its indefinite article, which belongs to the nominal it determines (rule 15).
Nomen rectum of סַל takes the of-relation (rule 19); unleavened bread for מַצָּה heads on unleavened, bread being the supplied generic (rule 31).

Nominal with no preposition and no object marker on it takes the ASV's supplied of, which states what it contributes (rule 33). Head on fine by rule 31's subtraction test: flour alone is any flour, exactly as land alone is any land in dry land and place alone is any place in high place. The class-noun tie-break does not reach it, since the ASV writes no bare flour in this verse or passage and its ordinary rendering of סֹלֶת is fine flour. Heading on flour as the class noun, with fine as a specifier, was the competing reading.
Assimilated article supplied by MACULA; the ASV writes no the for this phrase (rules 12, 29).
Assimilated article with no the written (rules 12, 29).
meal offering for מִנְחָה, headed on meal, offering being the supplied generic (rule 31).
drink offerings for נֶסֶךְ, headed on drink (rule 31).

review_notes: Corrected: the target head of סֹלֶת → of fine flour moves from flour to fine. Rule 31's subtraction test heads an adjective-plus-generic phrase on the modifier (dry land → dry, high place → high, burnt offerings → burnt), and its class-noun tie-break requires the bare noun in the verse, in the passage, or as the ordinary rendering of the word before you — the ASV writes no bare flour here and always renders סֹלֶת fine flour. The change also aligns the unit with unleavened bread → unleavened and meal offering → meal in the same verse. Heading on flour remains the named competing reading.

סֹלֶת carries no preposition and no object marker, and the ASV writes of before its own word, so the supplied of is that nominal's own under rule 33. MACULA tags סֹלֶת construct with חַלֹּת as its rectum, so rule 19 would instead put the of on חַלֹּת; rule 33 was taken because the ASV inverts the direction of the relation and writes the of before the construct noun rather than before the rectum.
Everything else in the verse is unchanged: both assimilated articles are unrepresented because no the is written, and the two attributive מַצּוֹת are read by rules 19 and 28 respectively.
